FINAL ORDER ON SUMMARY JUDGMENT
The Administra(cid:415)ve Law Judge (“ALJ”) Vanessa Voigt Gould, having reviewed the record
and Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner Oakland Holdings, LLC’s (“Oakland”) Mo(cid:415)on for Summary Judgment, brief in
support, designa(cid:415)on of evidence, and reply, as well as Respondents’ responses in opposi(cid:415)on and
counter designa(cid:415)ons, now issues this Final Order on Summary Judgment as it relates to the
Indiana Department of Environmental Management’s (“IDEM”) gran(cid:415)ng of Industrial Waste
Products Compos(cid:415)ng and Marke(cid:415)ng and Distribu(cid:415)on Permit No. IN LA 000909 (the “Permit”).
Any aggrieved party may appeal this decision. Appeal instruc(cid:415)ons are at the end of this
document.
Jurisdic(cid:415)on
The ALJ assigned to this proceeding by the Director of the Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law
Proceedings (“OALP”), see Ind. Code § 4-15-10.5-13, has jurisdic(cid:415)on over this case pursuant to
Indiana Code § 4-15-10.5-12, which gives OALP jurisdic(cid:415)on over agency administra(cid:415)ve ac(cid:415)ons
subject to the Indiana Administra(cid:415)ve Orders and Procedures Act at Indiana Code Art. 4-21.5
(“AOPA”) or “any other statute that requires or allows the office to take ac(cid:415)on.” The OALP has
jurisdic(cid:415)on over this case because this case is governed by AOPA.

Issues
The following issues were presented by the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner, Oakland Holdings, LLC (“Oakland”)
on Summary Judgment:
1. Whether the Permit unlawfully allows Organics to construct and operate a solid waste
processing facility without a solid waste processing permit in viola(cid:415)on of 329 IAC 11-9.
2. Whether the Permit unlawfully allows Organics to construct and operate a compost facility
without a compos(cid:415)ng facility registra(cid:415)on in viola(cid:415)on of Indiana Code § 13-20-10-2.
3. Whether the Permit violates Ind. Code § 13-20-10-9.
4. Whether the Permit violates 327 IAC 6.1-5-3.
5. Whether the Permit violates 327 IAC 6.1-5-2.
6. Whether IDEM’s applica(cid:415)on of the Land Applica(cid:415)on Rule and default standards in issuing the
Permit was arbitrary and/or unlawful.
7. Whether the Permit violates Indiana Code § 13-18-12-2.5.
8. Whether the Permit violates 327 IAC 6.1-8-6.
9. Whether the Permit violates Indiana Code § 13-15-4-1.

Findings of Fact
1. The Findings of Fact stated herein are undisputed.
2. On February 22, 2023, Organics submi(cid:425)ed a marke(cid:415)ng and distribu(cid:415)on permit applica(cid:415)on to
IDEM (“Applica(cid:415)on”) under 327 IAC 6.1-5.2
3. Through the Applica(cid:415)on, Organics sought IDEM approval to construct a compost facility at
3155 Wesley Road, Boonville, Warrick County, Indiana (“Site”), receive and process and/or
compost industrial waste product and other materials, and market and distribute the finished
compost as a landscaping or soil amendment.3
4. The Site is adjacent to real property owned by Oakland that has been approved for a primary
plat for a residen(cid:415)al subdivision containing 57 lots. Oakland maintains its property will be
adversely impacted by Organics’ construc(cid:415)on and opera(cid:415)on of the Site under the Permit.4

industrial waste products would be stored at the Site: (1) slope; (2) the water table; (3) soil
pH. The Applica(cid:415)on also did not contain any analy(cid:415)cal tes(cid:415)ng results or laboratory analysis
for the industrial waste products that would be received at the Site for processing and/or
compos(cid:415)ng.6

table where industrial waste will be stored at the Site.15
15. The purpose of the water table informa(cid:415)on being required in a management plan is to
determine whether the water table below the base of any storage structures will need to be
ar(cid:415)ficially lowered so as not to compromise the integrity of any permi(cid:425)ed storage
structures.16
16. During the permi(cid:427)ng process, Organics did not provide IDEM with soil-boring data or the soil
pH where the industrial waste will be stored at the Site.17
17. IDEM is unsure of the purpose of soil pH being required in a management plan and believes
it is irrelevant in terms of the Permit because all industrial waste products at the Site will be
stored on asphalts pads and not in direct contact with the soil.18
18. IDEM generally requires slopes, water table informa(cid:415)on, and soil borings to be submi(cid:425)ed with
the applica(cid:415)on during the permi(cid:427)ng process and before a Permit is approved and/or issued.19

dewatered; (2) meet the heavy metal limits detailed in Table 3 in 327 IAC 6.1-4-9(c); or (3)
meet the Polychlorinated Biphenyl (“PCB”) limit of 2 milligrams per kilogram on a dry weight

21. On November 20, 2023, IDEM approved the Applica(cid:415)on and issued Industrial Waste Products
Compos(cid:415)ng and Marke(cid:415)ng and Distribu(cid:415)on Permit No. IN LA 000909 to Organics (the
“Permit”).22
22. The Permit was issued pursuant to 327 IAC 6.1-5, which falls under IDEM’s Land Applica(cid:415)on
of Biosolid, Industrial Waste Product, and Pollutant-Bearing Water Rule, 327 IAC 6.1 (the
“Land Applica(cid:415)on Rule”).23
23. Upon receipt of an applica(cid:415)on for a marke(cid:415)ng and distribu(cid:415)on permit, IDEM reviews the
informa(cid:415)on provided and determines what statutes, rules, and standards are relevant and/or
apply.24
24. In certain instances, the Land Applica(cid:415)on Rule does not prescribe the specific standards to be
applied by IDEM in issuing a marke(cid:415)ng and distribu(cid:415)on permit.25
25. In the absence of specific statutory or regulatory standards, in its review and issuance of
marke(cid:415)ng permits, IDEM has developed default standards based on and consistent with other
regulatory programs, rules, and regula(cid:415)ons.26
26. These default standards require all industrial waste products to be stored on asphalt pads that
are sufficiently impermeable to prevent seepage into the soil and or groundwater, and that
all run off be contained on-site to prevent impact to surface waters.27
27. IDEM has applied these default standards to marke(cid:415)ng and distribu(cid:415)on permits as a means
of ensuring storage structures at a marke(cid:415)ng and distribu(cid:415)on facility protect human health
and the environment.28
28. These standards are comparable and consistent with regulatory standards imposed under
other regulatory programs and more specifically under certain solid waste rules and confined
feeding rules.29
29. The Permit was to be effec(cid:415)ve on issuance unless stayed through an appeal ac(cid:415)on.30

30. The Permit allows Organics to construct and operate a compos(cid:415)ng facility at the Site.31
31. The compos(cid:415)ng facility authorized under the Permit has not yet been constructed and is
thereby not yet opera(cid:415)onal.32
32. The Permit allows Organics to accept approximately 10,000 dry tons of industrial waste
product from a Pra(cid:425) Industries facility located in Henderson, Kentucky (“Kentucky Pra(cid:425)
Facility”) at the Site.33
33. Pra(cid:425) Industries is a paper recycler. The industrial waste product being imported from the
Kentucky Pra(cid:425) Facility (“Kentucky Industrial Waste Product”) is a solid waste and/or industrial
waste product that consists mainly of cellulose materials and/or cellulose fibers generated as
a byproduct of recycling of paper.34
34. The Permit also allows Organics to accept natural wood waste, yard waste (including limbs,
leaves, and grass), manures, spent feeds, straw, and pre- and post-consumer food waste at
the Site.35
35. The Permit also allows Organics to accept other industrial waste products at the Site upon
prior approval by IDEM.36
36. The Permit allows for the materials received by Organics to undergo a compos(cid:415)ng process, as
described in the Applica(cid:415)on, Management Plan, and Master Opera(cid:415)on Plan – at the Site.37
37. During the compos(cid:415)ng process the Kentucky Industrial Waste Product will be deposited in
long windrows and combined with other compostable materials approved by IDEM under the
Permit.38 The combined materials will then be turned, kept moist, and allowed to cure for a
period of approximately twelve to eighteen months.39

38. The Permit allows Organics to market and/or distribute the final or finished compost as a
landscaping or soil amendment, provided it complies with 327 IAC 6.1 and the Permit’s
specific requirements.40
39. The Permit imposes detailed requirements upon Organics related to the construc(cid:415)on,
opera(cid:415)on, safety, record keeping, monitoring, and compliance that are derived from the
applicable statutes, rules, and regula(cid:415)ons.41
40. The Permit allows for the construc(cid:415)on and maintenance of mul(cid:415)ple storage structures at the
Site including asphalt pads, a reten(cid:415)on pond or lagoon, and swale to direct and capture
stormwater, runoff, or any other liquid that may come in contact with the materials at the
Site.42
41. Under the Permit, all compos(cid:415)ng, curing, and storage of materials at the Site must take place
on the asphalt pads.43 This prevents the materials at the Site from coming into direct contact
with the soil.44
42. The permi(cid:425)ed storage structures at the Site are designed to prevent seepage of stormwater,
runoff, or any other liquid that may come in contact with the materials at the Site into the soil
and groundwater.45
43. The Permit sets construc(cid:415)on requirements and/or specifica(cid:415)ons for each of the permi(cid:425)ed
storage structures.46
44. The Permit requires Organics to submit documenta(cid:415)on, including photographs to
demonstrate compliance with said requirements once the storage structures are constructed
and before Organics begins opera(cid:415)ons at the Site.47
45. The Permit also requires Organics to measure the depth to the seasonal high water table as
determined by a registered professional soil scien(cid:415)st before construc(cid:415)ng the asphalt pads
and/or reten(cid:415)on pond or lagoon.48

48. Organics is required under the Permit to promptly correct and/or take remedial ac(cid:415)on if any

49. The Permit also sets specific pollutant concentra(cid:415)on limits and tes(cid:415)ng requirements -
including heavy metals and PCB limits - for all incoming solid waste and/or industrial waste
products and for all outgoing final or finished compost.52
50. The pollutant and PCB limits contained in the Permit are iden(cid:415)cal to those required under 327
IAC 6.1-5-2 as established by 327 IAC 6.1-4-9.53
51. Prior to accep(cid:415)ng any solid waste and/or industrial waste product at the Site, the Permit
requires Organics to sample the material for arsenic, cadmium, copper, lead, nickel, mercury,
molybdenum, selenium, zinc, PCBs, and Percent Total Solids.54
52. Prior to accep(cid:415)ng or compos(cid:415)ng any solid waste and/or industrial waste products at the Site,
Organics must also verify that the solid waste and/or industrial waste product has been
determined, in accordance with 329 IAC 3.1, to be non-hazardous.55
53. The Permit requires that before Organics can market or distribute the final or finished
